Hi all - quick security/infra notes after reviewing the call summary and template. I'll provide a short write-up for the MAP and a redlined network diagram. High level answers below: 

1) Data residency: For Private (customer-managed VPC) deployments in public cloud, we can ensure that storage and backups are provisioned in the customer-chosen region (us-east-1). We will document the S3 bucket/volume ARNs in the SOW. On-prem deployments obviously keep everything customer-side.

2) Egress: We support three primary modes:
   - Managed control plane (standard): requires limited outbound to Redwood-managed update and control endpoints. Endpoints can be whitelisted; we will provide IP ranges and FQDNs.
   - VPC-hosted Private: can operate with restricted egress - only to whitelisted endpoints (for telemetry/updates) or via customer-controlled NAT/proxy.
   - Air-gapped / on-prem: Full no-egress mode is supported for air-gapped installs; this requires an initial offline install package and an agreed update cadence for patches (we provide signed binaries).

3) Audit logging & retention: Audit logs, request/response logs, and model inference traces can be retained per-customer. Default retention is 90 days; configurable ranges of 7 days - 7 years can be negotiated in the contract. Customers may also stream logs to their SIEM (CloudWatch, Splunk, Datadog) via push or pull connectors - we'll include syslog/HTTPS connectors.

4) KMS/HSM: We support customer-managed KMS keys (AWS KMS/Cloud KMS) for at-rest encryption and can integrate with HSMs in on-prem deployments. Keys stay in the customer's KMS; Redwood has no plaintext access when CMK is used (we support envelope encryption patterns).

5) PII handling / redaction: Recommended approach for PHI workloads:
   - Prefer client-side redaction/tokenization for the strictest control (tokenize or hash identifiers before sending).
   - If client-side redaction is not feasible, server-side redaction modules can be enabled; these run in-customer VPC and can redact per configured rules before persistent storage.
   - KV cache handling: we recommend TTLs and encryption; avoid long-lived caches for PHI unless encrypted with CMK.

- Provide the list of IP ranges / FQDNs for minimal whitelist (ETA: 2026-03-26).
- Draft SOW language for retention/KMS/HSM options (ETA: 2026-03-27).
